sources.citation: Gordaliza, Th. 1908. Estudio sobre el dialecto Thô de la región de Lang-sơn. Anthropos 3: 512-532.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Calls Thô 'monosilábico'; section 'III. De la entonación' describes five 'tonos ó acentos' (llano, descendente, alto, interrogativo, grave) marked with quốc-ngữ-style diacritics; 'acento' is used only for tone marks and once for prominence within the diphthong âi; nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Sầm Công Danh. 2024. Một số nhận xét bước đầu về ngữ âm tiếng Tày Mường Bo (Sa Pa, Lào Cai) [Preliminary remarks on the phonology of Tày Mường Bo]. Journal of Science and Technology - HaUI. doi:10.57001/huih5804.2024.429
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Consonants, vowels, Gedney tone-box tones of Tày Sa Pa; nothing on trọng âm. NB this variety is Glottolog tays1238 (Tày Sa Pa, Southwestern Tai), not tayy1238.

sources.citation: Pittayaporn, Pittayawat & James Kirby. 2017. Laryngeal contrasts in the Tai dialect of Cao Bằng. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 47(1): 65-85. doi:10.1017/S0025100316000293
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Acoustic study of onset voicing, VOT, voice quality and the six-tone system of Cao Bằng Tai (Tày); monosyllabic stimuli; no statement about word stress (the only 'stress' token is the verb 'we stress that').

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. (n.d., archived 2012). Lesser Known Indigenous Languages of Northern Vietnam: map & language descriptions (ling.uta.edu/~jerry/research/, the Internet Archive 2012-02-07).
sources.note: Short notes on Tày Trung Khánh and Tày Bảo Lạc (voiced initials in low tones, tone values); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Vương Toàn. 1992. The Tay-Nung language in contact with the Vietnamese. Pan-Asiatic Linguistics: Proceedings of the 3rd International Symposium on Language and Linguistics, Bangkok: Chulalongkorn University, 909-919.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Loanword adaptation (vowel alternations, tone substitution for Vietnamese ngã); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hoàng Văn Ma, Lục Văn Pảo & Hoàng Chí (Nhóm Tày-Nùng, Viện Ngôn ngữ học). 1971. Ngữ pháp tiếng Tày-Nùng. Hà Nội: NXB Khoa học Xã hội. 152 pp. (archive.org stk.nguphaptiengtaynung)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Chương II 'Ngữ âm' (pp. 15-25) treats articulators, syllable template (âm đầu/âm đệm/âm gốc/âm cuối + thanh điệu), 11+3 vowels, consonants, six tones (§6 p. 24: bằng, sắc, huyền, hỏi, nặng, lửng) and tone-rhyme co-occurrence; the term 'trọng âm' (stress) never occurs; the reduplication section (pp. 39-41) mentions only 'ngữ điệu bình thường' (normal intonation) vs emphatic lengthening. Silent on word stress.

sources.citation: Diguet, Édouard. 1910. Étude de la langue thô (book edition of 'Éléments de grammaire thô et vocabulaire', Revue coloniale 1909-1911). Paris. Gallica ark:/12148/bd6t5358127n.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. I 'De la prononciation' (letters, vowel length) and Ch. II 'De l'intonation' (Cao Bằng Thô has six tons: supérieur, moyen, inférieur, ascendant étendu, ascendant supérieur, guttural, 'tout simplement ceux de la langue annamite'); 'accent' refers only to tone diacritics; no word-stress statement. Gallica full-text search for 'tonique', 'accentuée', 'appuy' returned no prosodic hits.
